campaign: Jetson AGX Thor (fp16) vs RTX 5090 (bf16) reference: FINE-TUNED GR00T closed-loop success-RATE + per-seed PARITY over the same 20-seed sweep and noise bank
reference: RTX-5090 bf16 reference run (same noise bank), win set [2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 11, 12, 14, 15] = 9/20

PARITY_headline.note: a flip = the board's precision changed a win/lose outcome vs the 5090 bf16 reference on the bit-identical scene+noise

in_loop_hz.note: in-loop Hz INCLUDES host<->board ZMQ network latency (client on host, policy on board); board_compute_hz is the board's get_action compute only (server-side timer).

caveats: 5090 reference is bf16, NOT fp32 -- part of any small residual is the 5090's own bf16.
Board attention runs on torch SDPA (no flash_attn on Jetson); SDPA is exact attention, far below the precision effect measured, and both boards use it consistently.
n=20 seeds; Wilson CI reflects the modest n.
Board runs the SAME fine-tuned policy brain as the 5090; flips are boundary disagreements, not capability.
verdict: Jetson AGX Thor (fp16) vs RTX 5090 (bf16): 10/20 = 50% success; agrees on 19/20 seeds, 1 FLIP(S) at [10]. Reference 9/20 = 45%. Arm-joint fidelity median 0.079. A flip is a win/lose disagreement on the bit-identical scene + noise -- report it plainly.
